prompt:
Find real, documented post-mortems of major cloud outages in 2025 (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud or Cloudflare). For each, cite the provider's own incident report and quote what it says the root cause was.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

If you're not sure about something, just say so.

response.content:
Here are four documented 2025 major cloud outages with official provider post-mortems:

**AWS — DynamoDB DNS disruption (US-EAST-1), October 19–20, 2025**

SOURCE: https://postmortem.io/incidents/aws--2025-10-19--dynamodb-dns-service-disruption-us-east-1/ | QUOTE: "The incident stemmed from a latent race condition in the DynamoDB DNS management system that resulted in an incorrect empty DNS record for the service’s regional endpoint." | CLAIM: AWS attributes the outage to a race condition in the DNS management system that created an empty DNS record.

SOURCE: https://postmortem.io/incidents/aws--2025-10-19--dynamodb-dns-service-disruption-us-east-1/ | QUOTE: "The race condition occurred when a delayed DNS Enactor applied an outdated plan that overwrote a newer plan, and the cleanup process then deleted the old plan, removing all IP addresses for the regional endpoint." | CLAIM: The specific mechanism involved a delayed DNS Enactor applying an outdated plan, which caused removal of all IP addresses for the regional endpoint.

**Microsoft Azure — Front Door global outage, October 29–30, 2025**

SOURCE: https://postmortem.io/incidents/azure--2025-10-29--azure-front-door-global-connectivity-dns-issues/ | QUOTE: "A specific sequence of customer configuration changes, performed across two different control plane build versions, resulted in incompatible customer configuration metadata being generated." | CLAIM: Azure attributes the outage to customer configuration changes across different control plane build versions that generated incompatible metadata.

SOURCE: https://postmortem.io/incidents/azure--2025-10-29--azure-front-door-global-connectivity-dns-issues/ | QUOTE: "This incompatibility triggered a crash during asynchronous processing within the data plane service. This defect escaped detection due to a gap in our pre-production validation, since not all features are validated across different control plane build versions." | CLAIM: The incompatible metadata crashed the data plane service, and the bug escaped detection due to incomplete pre-production validation across build versions.

**Cloudflare — Network outage, November 18, 2025**

SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/18-november-2025-outage/ | QUOTE: "Instead, it was triggered by a change to one of our database systems' permissions which caused the database to output multiple entries into a “feature file” used by our Bot Management system. That feature file, in turn, doubled in size." | CLAIM: Cloudflare attributes the outage to a database permissions change that caused the Bot Management feature file to double in size.

SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/18-november-2025-outage/ | QUOTE: "The software running on these machines to route traffic across our network reads this feature file to keep our Bot Management system up to date with ever changing threats. The software had a limit on the size of the feature file that was below its doubled size. That caused the software to fail." | CLAIM: The oversized feature file exceeded the routing software's size limit, causing the network failure.

**Cloudflare — Dashboard and API outage, September 12, 2025**

SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/deep-dive-into-cloudflares-sept-12-dashboard-and-api-outage/ | QUOTE: "The incident’s impact stemmed from several issues, but the immediate trigger was a bug in the dashboard. This bug caused repeated, unnecessary calls to the Tenant Service API." | CLAIM: Cloudflare attributes the outage to a dashboard bug that caused repeated, unnecessary API calls to the Tenant Service.

SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/deep-dive-into-cloudflares-sept-12-dashboard-and-api-outage/ | QUOTE: "The API calls were managed by a React useEffect hook, but we mistakenly included a problematic object in its dependency array. Because this object was recreated on every state or prop change, React treated it as “always new,” causing the useEffect to re-run each time." | CLAIM: The specific bug was a React useEffect hook with an object in the dependency array that was recreated on every state change, causing infinite re-renders and API calls.

**Cloudflare — Network outage, December 5, 2025**

SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/5-december-2025-outage/ | QUOTE: "Instead, it was triggered by changes being made to our body parsing logic while attempting to detect and mitigate an industry-wide vulnerability disclosed this week in React Server Components." | CLAIM: Cloudflare attributes the outage to changes in body parsing logic intended to mitigate a React Server Components vulnerability.

SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/5-december-2025-outage/ | QUOTE: "Unfortunately, in our FL1 version of our proxy, under certain circumstances, the second change of turning off our WAF rule testing tool caused an error state that resulted in 500 HTTP error codes to be served from our network." | CLAIM: A secondary change to turn off a WAF rule testing tool caused an error state in the FL1 proxy, resulting in 500 errors.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Any Google Cloud major outage post-mortem for 2025.
